name: Francis Rooney
role: U.S. representative from Florida, 2017–2021; ambassador to the Holy See, 2005–2008
summary: Rooney combines private-sector economics and socially conservative positions with carbon pricing, ocean protection and support for raising the minimum wage. His later statements defend constitutional restraints, professional diplomacy and military partnerships while criticizing aspects of Trump’s leadership.

universal-healthcare.rationale: At his 2017 town hall he defended rejecting universal government provision, contrasting it unfavorably with the French system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Introduced an indexed $8.50 floor and then voted for the larger $15 phased increase; the latter vote establishes substantial support.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Explicitly preferred private-sector solutions over government provision.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Criticized high marginal rates, including the 39.6 percent top bracket, and advocated lower income taxes.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Welcomed renewed rules on energy production, offshore drilling, mercury and methane.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Explicitly opposed legalizing and regulating marijuana; other drugs unspecified.

strong-leader.rationale: Warned against a personality cult and defended constitutional restraints on presidential power.

limit-guns.rationale: Proposed restrictions in 2018, voted against universal background-check legislation in 2019, and later criticized his party’s gun position; precise current limits remain mixed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said the United States lacks enough ships and needs credible military strength around Taiwan.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Rejected legal marriage definitions beyond one man and one woman.

abortion-legal.rationale: Answered that abortion should be permitted under no circumstances.

more-religion-public.rationale: Promised to defend faith and Christian values in national life.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Personally introduced RAISE legislation to reduce legal admissions and restrict family and refugee categories, while seeking skilled workers.

free-trade.rationale: Said interconnected trade benefits developed and developing economies, consumers and international stability.

open-borders.rationale: Supported border walls, controlled admissions and narrow asylum eligibility.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate threats severe and backed carbon pricing plus restored energy regulations.

central-planning.rationale: His explicit preference for private-sector solutions over government direction weighs against a centrally planned economy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Recalled promoting separation of church and state as an American value in his diplomatic work.

military-superiority.rationale: Demanded nuclear superiority and later warned of inadequate naval strength.

taxation-theft.rationale: Advocated a fairer tax system and legitimate carbon taxation rather than treating every tax as theft.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Earlier favored fewer oil restrictions with a Florida exception; later opposed new offshore drilling and sought to price coal out.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Criticized entrenched officials who prioritize themselves and their continued tenure over constituents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Personally proposed wage regulation and supported environmental intervention beyond security, justice and property enforcement.

separated-powers.rationale: Insisted Congress exercise constitutional authority to authorize war rather than surrendering it to the president.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Urged continued South Korean military exercises and support for Ukraine against Russia.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Supported FADA protections for religious objections to same-sex marriage.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Explicitly supported the United States maintaining its own nuclear arsenal.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Praised interconnected global trade rather than closing economies into self-sufficient blocs.

delink-world-market.rationale: Explicitly included developing countries among the beneficiaries of globalized trade.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argued that lobbying prowess determines too many special-interest tax breaks.

non-intervention.rationale: Said hard power sometimes is necessary and praised the Venezuela operation, while criticizing the Iran campaign’s execution.

assisted-dying.rationale: Endorsed legal protection of life through natural death; a broad position, not a detailed assisted-dying statute.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ranked God above Constitution and voters as authority sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Called for maintaining modern nuclear forces and sustaining allied military exercises.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Advocated active security partnerships against Chinese and Russian pressure.

term-limits.rationale: Personally sponsored congressional term limits and renewed that advocacy in 2026.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Endorsed force abroad beyond repelling an immediate attack, including the Venezuela operation.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Explicitly advocated carbon pricing to remove high-emitting fuels.

future-generations.rationale: Committed to protecting oceans for generations to come.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Supported retaining a modern arsenal superior to potential adversaries.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cosponsored repeal of federal provisions allowing dismissal for refusing union dues or fees.

voter-id.rationale: Rejected voting without photographic identification; citizenship-proof details unspecified.

close-ties-china.rationale: Criticized deference to China and sought credible resistance to pressure on Taiwan and regional partners.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Condemned lobbying-driven tax carve-outs, ethanol subsidies and special-interest favors.

notes: Candidate answers are his own, not the voter guide’s ideological rating. Later wage and environmental positions supersede broad early campaign opposition where specific. Gun evidence remains mixed. Religious belief does not establish scriptural law, criminalization of homosexuality or opposition to every form of religious freedom. Support for defending Israel establishes no specific territorial or Palestinian policy. General school choice does not establish a particular voucher program. Constitutional war powers do not imply absolute nonintervention; he approved some uses of force and criticized others. Host statements in 2026 interviews are excluded. Support for Ukraine’s government is not support for foreign insurgents. The 2019 labor questions criticize union abuses without establishing opposition to collective bargaining itself. Reviewed all remaining nulls across ten themes, including technology and personal liberties; no inference from party, Catholic identity, business holdings or associates.
